mappedContracts.statement: Create a canonical machine-readable implementation contract derived from this prompt and make it the binding source of truth for all subsequent work.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract records this prompt's SHA-256, every contract ID, phase, track, task, dependency decision, acceptance criterion, GitHub issue reference, Conductor path, status, evidence, and exception.
A deterministic validator fails on missing mappings, duplicate IDs, invalid states, orphaned tasks, unapproved scope changes, or completion without evidence.
Every implementation PR runs the contract validator as a required check.

mappedContracts.statement: Integrate the current edithatogo/repository-standards system and inherit its latest applicable node/software, supply-chain, coverage, release, verification-receipt, and solo-maintainer controls.
acceptanceCriteria: The repository is registered or refreshed in repository-standards with the correct profile and risk posture.
Centrally managed files are not forked silently; repository-owned deviations are explicit exceptions.
The one-command verification receipt conforms to the current repository-standards schema.
The model remains operable by one maintainer with zero mandatory human approvals and strong automated gates.

mappedContracts.statement: Inspect every direct dependency and runtime for relevant experimental APIs, flags, transports, extensions, performance controls, and security features; adopt all relevant features in mainline.
acceptanceCriteria: The adoption manifest records package, resolved version, upstream source, experimental feature, relevance assessment, adopted implementation, tests, and rollback.
A feature may be excluded only if irrelevant, removed upstream, mutually incompatible, or demonstrably unsafe; every exclusion requires an evidence-backed contract exception.
Capability negotiation or safety policy may control runtime use, but the implementation remains present and tested in mainline.

mappedContracts.statement: Provide lossless export, import, backup, verification, restore, and rollback for local state and recoverable Substack content.
acceptanceCriteria: Backups are versioned, checksummed, portable, privacy-aware, and restorable in a clean environment.
Restore validates schema and hash chain before replacing state.
Disaster-recovery drills are automated.

mappedContracts.statement: Replace misleading headline coverage with risk-weighted assurance and remove blanket exclusions from high-risk modules.
acceptanceCriteria: Credential, authorization, policy, planning, mutation, state, media, billing, subscriber, team, and MCP HTTP code has explicit branch and mutation targets.
Coverage exclusions require contract exceptions.
Issue #161 is reused and completed.

mappedContracts.statement: Use property-based, model-based, fuzz, mutation, differential, metamorphic, contract, concurrency, fault-injection, and snapshot testing where warranted.
acceptanceCriteria: Parsers, paths, plans, schedules, redaction, state machines, tasks, and transport recovery receive advanced testing.
Fuzz failures are minimized and retained as regression fixtures.
Mutation score thresholds are risk-specific and blocking.

mappedContracts.statement: Provide one deterministic verification command that runs contracts, generation drift, types, lint, tests, coverage, mutation, fuzz smoke, package checks, MCP conformance, security checks, and receipt generation.
acceptanceCriteria: The command works locally and in CI.
It emits a machine-readable verification receipt conforming to repository-standards.
Release consumes the same verified artefacts rather than rebuilding differently.
